Quick Remediation Plan

Highest pressure areas: Anomalies (97%), Privileged Accounts (95%), Stale Objects (51%). Follow the steps below to reduce risk in order.

  1. Anomalies (97%): Investigate unusual identity/permission patterns and close unintended paths that allow privilege escalation.
  2. Privileged Accounts (95%): Reduce standing privilege: remove unnecessary admin rights, enforce PAW/JIT model, and rotate privileged credentials.
  3. Stale Objects (51%): Disable and clean stale users/computers after business validation to shrink attack surface.
  4. Validate and close: re-run this report after remediation and confirm Critical/High findings trend downward.

Immediate focus (Critical/High):

  • [Critical] krbtgt password age - Rotate krbtgt password in a controlled 2-step process and document rotation cadence.
  • [Critical] Tier0: Dangerous ACE on critical objects - Remove non-essential GenericAll/GenericWrite/WriteDacl/WriteOwner ACEs from Tier-0 objects.
  • [Critical] Privileged Review: Administrators - Builtin Administrators grants extensive control on domain controllers and critical systems.
  • [Critical] Privileged Review: Domain Admins - Domain-wide administrative rights should be tightly limited and controlled.
  • [Critical] Privileged Review: Schema Admins - Schema changes are high-impact and should be temporary, approved and audited.

Admin Privilege Tiers

Microsoft Tier Model — analyzes separation between identity infrastructure, servers, and end users.

Score
Critical: 2 Warning: 6 Info: 3 OK: 7
What Is the AD Tier Model?
Microsoft's Administrative Tier Model splits Active Directory into 3 isolated security layers. The goal: a compromised user workstation must never give an attacker a path to Domain Admin. Each tier requires dedicated accounts, separate GPOs, and logon restrictions.
DOMAIN CORE — MOST CRITICAL
AD, Domain Controllers & Identity
Critical • 2 critical • 3 warnings
CRITICALPrivileged accounts in default CN=Users container
4 affected

Domain Admins, Schema Admins, or Enterprise Admins accounts reside in the default CN=Users container. These accounts should be in a dedicated Tier 0 OU with restricted GPO and access controls.

Administrator
svcexchange
ekaya
mkoc
What To Do
Create a dedicated 'Tier 0 Admins' OU (e.g., OU=T0-Admins,OU=Admin,DC=...) and move all privileged accounts there. Apply a restrictive GPO blocking internet access and enforcing logon restrictions.
WARNINGNo dedicated Tier 0 / Admin OU detected

No OU with naming patterns like 'Admin', 'Tier0', 'Privileged', or 'T0-' was found. A dedicated administrative OU is a Tier Model prerequisite for applying strict access controls and GPOs to privileged accounts.

What To Do
Create OU=Administration with sub-OUs: OU=T0-Admins, OU=T1-Admins, OU=T2-Admins. Apply Logon Restriction GPOs to each tier's OU.
OKDomain Admins count acceptable (5 members)

Domain Admins group has 5 member(s), which is within the recommended range of 2-5.

What To Do
Continue to audit Domain Admin membership periodically.
WARNINGProtected Users group is empty
5 affected

The Protected Users security group has no members. This group enforces Kerberos-only authentication, prevents NTLM, disables credential caching, and enforces AES encryption for Tier 0 accounts.

Administrator
svcexchange
mkoc
ekaya
svchelpdesk
What To Do
Add all Domain Admins, Schema Admins, and Enterprise Admins to the Protected Users group. Test compatibility before broad rollout.
WARNINGNo fine-grained password policy (PSO) configured
1 affected

No Fine-Grained Password Policy with MinPasswordLength >= 20 was found. Tier 0 accounts require stricter password policies than the domain default to resist brute force and credential stuffing.

No PSO found
What To Do
Create a PSO with MinPasswordLength=20, LockoutThreshold=3, and ComplexityEnabled=True. Apply it to Domain Admins and other Tier 0 accounts via a global security group.
CRITICALkrbtgt password not rotated in 833 days (>180)
1 affected

The krbtgt account password is 833 days old. This account's password is used to encrypt all Kerberos tickets. If compromised (Golden Ticket attack), an attacker can forge tickets for any account. Rotation every 180 days is the minimum standard.

krbtgt: 833 days old
What To Do
Rotate the krbtgt password using a two-step process (rotate twice, 10 hours apart) to invalidate any forged tickets. Use Microsoft's New-KrbtgtKeys.ps1 script.
